requirement:
HC represents a FIXME acknowledgment as a graph node and exposes its tracking
issue relationships as labeled edges to GitHub issue nodes. A named FIXME also
connects the acknowledgment to the requirement whose gap it acknowledges;
an unnamed FIXME connects directly to its tracking issues.
Each issue named by the acknowledgment is available through its tracking edges.
rationale:
`requirements.sdk.habeas.fixme_graph` has no `{test}` references or `:test:` anchors. The `references` tool lists no sites for it, and a text search for `fixme_graph` finds only the requirement's own declaration and the `{fixme}` comment on `src/sdk.rs#enum[HabeasNode]`.

The requirement has four obligations. None has a test:
- A FIXME acknowledgment is a graph node.
- Its tracking issues are exposed as labeled edges to GitHub issue nodes.
- A named FIXME also connects to the requirement whose gap it acknowledges.
- An unnamed FIXME connects directly to its tracking issues, and every issue it names is available through those edges.

Edge labeling exists in `src/sdk.rs#impl[HabeasDomain<'_>/Domain]/fn[outgoing_edges]`. The only test text I found there is `domain_storage_round_trips_each_review_kind_and_preserves_records_on_errors`, which stores `fixmes: []` as data and does not exercise this requirement.

The gap is acknowledged. The `{fixme} requirements.sdk.habeas.fixme_graph` on `src/sdk.rs#enum[HabeasNode]` names `nikomatsakis/habeas-codicem#26`, which is open. Its body says the graph nodes and tracking-issue edges are deferred and that named and unnamed acknowledgments, source ownership, and multiple issue targets have no tests. That is the same missing-test gap I found, so it is acknowledged.
